summary.body:
Design systems engineer with **eleven years** of shipping component libraries that survive contact with real product teams. I work at the seam between design and engineering: tokens, accessibility, and the tooling that keeps both honest.

Currently leading *Halo*, the design system behind every Lumen Health surface. I write about the craft at [okafor.design/notes](https://okafor.design/notes).

items.summary:
Own **Halo**, the design system behind every Lumen Health surface: the web console, the clinician tablet app, and the patient mobile app.

- Rebuilt the token pipeline so design and code read from a single source, cutting drift reports from roughly fourteen per quarter to two
  - Shipped a *codemod* that migrated 1,100 hard-coded colour values in one review
  - Added contrast assertions to CI, which now block any token pair below 4.5:1
- Wrote the [Halo contribution guide](https://halo.lumenhealth.io/contributing); outside contributions rose from three to thirty-one in a year
- Led the remediation that took the clinician tablet app to **WCAG 2.2 AA**, verified by an external audit in January 2025

Team: four engineers.  
Review load: around sixty component pull requests per quarter.

Led the rewrite of Northbeam's reporting console from a jQuery monolith to a typed React application, delivered in three phases without a feature freeze.

1. Split the monolith into nine route-level bundles, taking first contentful paint from 4.8s to 1.3s on a throttled 3G profile
2. Introduced *contract tests* against the reporting API, which caught twenty-three breaking changes before release
3. Handed the resulting patterns to the platform team as Northbeam's first shared component library

Also mentored two engineers through their first year; both are still shipping.

Built marketing sites and small product front-ends for agency clients: *fast turnarounds, unforgiving briefs*.

- Delivered more than twenty client projects, several on two-week timelines
- Set up the studio's first shared **Sass toolkit**, which ended the habit of copying the previous project's stylesheet

Dissertation on **perceptual colour spaces for data visualisation**, supervised by Dr. Helen Marsh.

- Course representative for the 2014-15 cohort
- Ran the department's weekly accessibility reading group

Taken part-time alongside full-time work. Coursework in *interaction design*, usability evaluation, and assistive technology.

The final project measured screen-reader task completion across three component library APIs and became the basis for a later conference talk.

items.name: TypeScript
items.description: The day-to-day language for **library code**. Comfortable with generic component APIs and the type-level work that keeps them ergonomic.

items.name: Design Tokens
items.description: Pipelines from design-tool variables to platform artefacts. Documented in the [Halo token spec](https://halo.lumenhealth.io/tokens).

items.name: Accessibility
items.description:
WCAG 2.2 AA in practice rather than in theory:

- Keyboard and focus-order review
- Screen reader passes with NVDA and VoiceOver
- Automated axe checks wired into CI

items.name: Rust
items.description: Reached for build tooling: a token compiler and a *considerably* faster SVG icon pipeline.

items.name: Contrastly
items.description: Browser extension for auditing colour contrast in **live** interfaces
items.summary:
Started as a debugging aid for the Halo remediation and grew into a small public tool.

1. Samples computed styles rather than design files, so it catches the blends that palettes miss
2. Reports failures against *both* WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 thresholds
3. Exports a CSV that plugs straight into an audit spreadsheet

Around 4,000 weekly active users.

items.name: tokenwright
items.description: *Zero-config* CLI that compiles design tokens to CSS, Swift, and Kotlin
items.summary:
Written in Rust after the Node build step became the slowest part of Halo's release.

- Full compile of 2,300 tokens went from 11s to under 400ms
- Emits a diff report so reviewers can see what a token change actually costs
- Ships as a single binary; see the [installation notes](https://github.com/mireilleokafor/tokenwright#install)

items.name: Tokens Are a Contract, Not a Palette
items.summary: Argues that a token set is an **API** with the same compatibility obligations as any other, and proposes a deprecation policy for teams that rename things too freely.

items.name: Auditing a Design System for WCAG 2.2
items.summary:
A write-up of the Halo audit, including the failures that automated tooling missed.

- Target size was the most common new 2.2 failure
- Focus appearance failures clustered in *composed* components rather than primitives

Coach at fortnightly workshops for people underrepresented in tech.

Usually paired with a student for a full term, working through HTML and CSS before moving on to their first JavaScript project.

items.title: Systems Craft Award
items.summary: Awarded for the Halo token pipeline, cited by the panel as *"the clearest worked example of tokens as versioned infrastructure"*.

items.title: Accessibility Advocate of the Year
items.summary: Community-nominated award recognising the **WCAG 2.2 audit write-up** and the open office hours that followed it.

items.name: Certified Professional in Accessibility Core Competencies
items.summary: The **CPACC** covers disability models, standards, and organisational policy. Verification is available through the [IAAP directory](https://www.accessibilityassociation.org/certification).

items.name: Professional Scrum Master I
items.summary: Taken during the Northbeam rewrite, mostly to *argue more precisely* about scope with the delivery team.

items.name: English
items.description: **Native.** Schooling and all professional work to date.

items.name: German
items.description: Working proficiency, retained from three years in Berlin.

items.name: Dr. Helen Marsh
items.summary: Contact details supplied on request, alongside a reference from my current engineering director.

items.title: Design Tokens Beyond Colour
items.subtitle: Clarity Conference
items.summary:
Forty minutes on what happens when a token set has to describe motion, elevation, and density rather than just colour.

- Why *semantic* naming breaks down at the third platform
- The versioning policy we adopted after two painful renames

Slides and a transcript are at [okafor.design/talks/beyond-colour](https://okafor.design/talks/beyond-colour).

items.title: Shipping Accessible Components by Default
items.subtitle: Front-End Lisbon
items.summary: A meetup talk on making the accessible path the **easy** path: sensible defaults, a focus-visible policy, and CI checks that fail loudly.

items.title: Maintaining a Design System with Four People
items.subtitle: Smashing Workshop
items.summary:
A half-day workshop, run twice, on the operational side of a small systems team.

1. Triage: what earns a place in the library and what stays in the product
2. Contribution: review turnaround as the *only* metric that matters
3. Deprecation: how to remove a component without breaking six teams

items.title: Technical Advisor
items.subtitle: Open Health UI Collective
items.summary: Quarterly review of the collective's shared patterns for clinical interfaces, with a standing focus on *colour-blind safe* status indicators.

items.title: Reviewer, Accessibility Track
items.subtitle: EuroFront
items.summary: Reviewed **sixty-odd** talk proposals across two years and mentored three first-time speakers through their outlines.
